seo_title: Ballroom Dance Academy Case Study: Content Strategy | SOMIN
description: SOMIN found rivals published 402 organic posts to Ballroom Dance Academy's 39 in 90 days, then built it a 3-pillar plan, a 39-post calendar and a paid funnel.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Dance education · Singapore
h1: Ballroom Dance Academy has a publishing problem, not a product problem
lede: Ballroom Dance Academy Singapore (BDAS) offers classes from a 4-week Beginner Taster to competitive DanceSport. SOMIN read 24 months of organic content from BDAS and 4 rival academies, plus 53 competitor Facebook ads. In the last 90 days rivals published 402 organic posts to BDAS's 39, and BDAS ran no ads. SOMIN built 3 pillars, a 39-post calendar and 4 paid ad concepts.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · Jun 2024 to May 2026 · Singapore

challenge.title: Ballroom Dance Academy's classes, out-shouted by 4 rivals
challenge.body: BDAS offers a full path of classes, from a 4-week Beginner Taster to competitive DanceSport, plus kids classes, wedding dance preparation and monthly socials. Yet it was being out-shouted in its own category, and 2 of its 4 competitors run Facebook ads while BDAS runs none. The question was where it could differentiate, reclaim ground and place a bet.

approach.title: Eight quarterly windows of organic content and 53 rival ads
points: Catalogued BDAS's real classes, programmes and events on ballroomdancesingapore.com, so the strategy extends what already exists.
Tracked organic content from BDAS and 4 competitors across 8 quarterly windows, June 2024 to May 2026, with year-over-year verification.
Compared brand and competitor share of voice by theme to find where BDAS can differentiate, reclaim or bet.
Read 53 competitor Facebook ads to map the paid beginner funnel BDAS is missing.
Built persona, tension, angle and story chains for 3 pillars, drawing on 11 SOMIN studies.

findings_title: Out-published ten to one and absent from paid beginner ads

findings.title: Out-published 402 posts to 39 in 90 days
findings.body: Competitors published 402 organic posts to BDAS's 39 in the last 90 days, leaving BDAS with about 9% of organic share of voice across the 5 academies.

findings.title: Teaching is 26.4% of rival content, 2.6% of BDAS's
findings.body: Dance education makes up 26.4% of competitor content but only 2.6% of BDAS's, even though its own tagline is 'An Academy of expert teaching and coaching.'

findings.title: Rival ads chase beginners, and BDAS runs none
findings.body: Competitor ads run a beginner-acquisition funnel: kids 43%, confidence 30% and 'anyone can dance' 23% of 53 ads. BDAS is absent from all of it.

delivered.title: Three pillars, 75 creative concepts and a 39-post calendar
points: 3 pillars: The Stage Where Dancers Get Seen, An Academy of Expert Teaching, and A Space for All (Anyone Can Dance)
9 propositions, 3 per pillar, each matched to a TOFU, MOFU or BOFU ad concept
75 creative concepts rendered as SOMIN images in the BDAS identity
A 13-week organic calendar of 39 posts at 3 a week, weighted Teaching 16, Recognition 14, Confidence 9
4 paid ad concepts routed to real pages for beginners, kids, classes and weddings

quote.text: Visibility is not BDAS's product problem — it is BDAS's publishing problem.

outcome.title: Ballroom Dance Academy's plan: 3 posts a week and a paid funnel
outcome.body: BDAS should move to a consistent 3-pillar, 3-posts-a-week rhythm, make expert teaching visible, and lean on its owned galas and championships, the one thing rivals can't copy. In paid, it can mirror the proven beginner funnel in its own elegant voice, leading with the 4-week Beginner Taster as the low-risk first step.

faq.a: The DanceSport Academy, Galaxy Dance Academy, Melvyn Low Dance Studio and Aquilia Dance Academy. Only Galaxy and The DanceSport Academy run Facebook ads.

faq.q: Why open a paid channel now?
faq.a: Rivals use paid to convert beginners with kids, confidence and 'anyone can dance' messages, the same emerging themes BDAS already has organic permission for. Every beginner search in Singapore currently meets a competitor ad, never BDAS.

No. Coverage was partial, with brand and competitor cohorts only and no audience-proxy cohort, so SOMIN labels themes as contested, blocked, emerging or partial rather than claiming confirmed whitespace.
